newsitem.title: PERU: Peru guerrillas attack jungle village, kill three.
newsitem.headline: Peru guerrillas attack jungle village, kill three.

text.p: About 60 guerrillas from the Maoist Shining Path group attacked a village in the Peruvian jungle and killed three members of a civil defence patrol organised to combat rebel activity, police said on Saturday.

During the attack on the village of San Jorge on Friday, "there was a clash that left three dead among the residents," said a police source from the nearby town of Tingo Maria, 250 miles (400 km) northeast of Lima.

The guerrillas took about 40 rifles, telecommunications equipment and identity documents from the San Jorge patrol, one of many civil organisations established in rural areas with army assistance to reduce vulnerability to rebel attacks. Police have not yet located the attackers.
Clashes that involve guerrillas and drug traffickers are common in the northeastern region of Huanuco, where the attack occurred.

Police said that another guerrilla ambush on a bridge in the area on Thursday left one policeman hurt, and on the same day in the town of Aucayacu, two drug-trafficking bands clashed, with a still unknown number of victims.

The army's anti-guerrilla operations are currently focused on the central Andes -- specifically Huancavelica, Junin and Ayacucho departments -- where 2,000 soldiers have been hunting for Shining Path's military leader Oscar Ramirez Durand, alias "Comrade Feliciano," since early September.

Guerrilla violence in the country, mainly from the Shining Path and the smaller Tupac Amaru Guerrilla Movement (MRTA), has killed 30,000 Peruvians and caused damages estimated to around $25 billion in 16 years.
